audio.title: Audio signals (orange jacks)
audio.what: A sound: a signal that swings between about -1 and +1 hundreds or thousands of times a second. Played through a speaker, it is what you hear.
audio.does: How fast it swings is the pitch; the shape of each swing is the tone (a saw sounds bright, a sine pure); how far it swings is the volume. Everything that makes or changes sound passes audio from module to module.
audio.why: Sound is the end product: every patch is a chain that makes audio (an oscillator, noise), shapes it (filter, VCA, effects) and sends it to the Output.
try: Right-click an orange output to see it on the scope: the shape you see is the shape you hear.
Plug an audio output into a modulation input (an oscillator into a filter's CUTOFF): modulation at audio speed makes new, rough tones.

pitch.title: Pitch signals (blue jacks)
pitch.what: A note, as a number: 1 per octave, 0 is middle C. +1 is the C above, -1 the C below, 1/12 is a semitone.
pitch.does: An oscillator turns pitch into a frequency: each +1 doubles it. Because the scale is in octaves, adding signals transposes: 0.583 (7 semitones) added to any note gives its fifth. That's why a sequencer's pitch plus your key's pitch plays the pattern from your key.
pitch.why: It is how notes travel through a patch: from your keyboard (MIDI In's PITCH) or a sequencer to the oscillators, and to a filter's KEY so the filter follows the notes.
try: Plug MIDI In's PITCH into an oscillator's PITCH and play: the oscillator follows.
Put a Slew between them: notes glide.
Plug an LFO into the oscillator's FM instead: the pitch wobbles.

gate.title: Gate signals (green jacks)
gate.what: On or off: 1 while something is happening (a key held, a clock tick), 0 when not. A very short gate is called a trigger.
gate.does: Modules that start things listen for the gate to rise from 0 to 1: an envelope starts its attack, a sequencer moves a step, a Sample & Hold takes a sample. Some also watch it fall: an envelope releases when the gate closes.
gate.why: Gates are the timing of a patch: when notes start and stop. Pitch says which note; the gate says when.
try: Plug MIDI In's GATE into a VCA's CV: the note switches on and off, with a click.
Plug it into an envelope's GATE instead, and the envelope into the VCA: the note fades in and out.

mod.title: Modulation signals (violet jacks)
mod.what: A control that changes slowly compared to sound: an envelope rising from 0 to 1 and falling back, an LFO swinging between -1 and +1, the mod wheel.
mod.does: Plugged into a module's input, it moves one of its settings for you, faster or more precisely than a hand on a knob: the cutoff of a filter, the volume of a VCA, the pitch of an oscillator. The input's amount knob sets how far.
mod.why: Movement is what makes synth sounds alive: a filter that opens on each note, vibrato, a tremolo, a wah. Modulation is how you get it.
try: Plug an LFO's OUT into a filter's CUTOFF and turn the filter's CV up: a wah.
Plug an envelope into the same CUTOFF instead: a sweep on every note.

add.title: + ADD MODULE
add.what: The list of every module Konnekt has, grouped by what they do: sources, filters, envelopes, modulation, utilities, effects, sequencing.
add.does: Click one and it appears in view on the rack, ready to drag where you want it and wire up. Right-click one in the list to read about it before adding it.
add.why: A modular synth starts empty: you choose the parts. Adding them one at a time and hearing what each does is the best way to learn them.
try: Start from lesson 1 and add one module at a time: a filter between the oscillator and the VCA, then an envelope for the filter.

voices.title: VOICES
voices.what: How many notes can sound at once, 1 to 8. The lights next to it show the notes being held.
voices.does: Modules that run per voice (oscillators, filters, envelopes, VCAs...) run once for each voice: every note gets its own oscillator, its own envelope. Modules that run once (effects, the clock, the Output) get all the voices mixed together.
voices.why: With 1 voice Konnekt is a monophonic synth, like a classic bass or lead: the newest key plays, and going back to a key still held doesn't restart the envelopes (legato). More voices let you play chords.
try: Set 1 for a bass part and play legato: hold one key, press another, let go of the second.

learn.title: LEARN (MIDI Learn)
learn.what: Links a knob on the screen to a knob or slider on your MIDI controller.
learn.does: Press LEARN: every knob gets a ring. Click one (its ring turns red), then move a knob on your controller: they're linked, and the screen knob shows the CC number. Right-click a ring to forget its link. LEARN again, or Esc, to finish.
learn.why: Turning a real knob while you play is how you hear what a control does, and it's how you perform with a patch. The links are saved with the patch.
try: Link a filter's CUTOFF and RESONANCE to two knobs and sweep them while playing.

patches.title: PATCHES
patches.what: Your saved racks: modules, where they sit, every knob, the cables, the voices and the MIDI links.
patches.does: Type a name and SAVE (the same name replaces it); click a name to load it, which replaces the rack; ✕ deletes one. The rack as you leave it also comes back next time you open Konnekt.
patches.why: Keep the sounds you make, and keep a working patch before you start taking it apart.

lessons.title: LESSONS
lessons.what: Ten patches that build a synth up a module at a time, each with what to listen for and what to try.
lessons.does: Each loads its patch (replacing the rack: save yours first) and opens its text at the bottom left, with ◂ ▸ to move between them.
lessons.why: They take you from one oscillator to filters, envelopes, LFOs, FM, sequencing and effects in order, each building on the last.
try: Load a lesson, then pull out one cable at a time and hear what each did.

help.title: HELP
help.what: Konnekt's manual: every module, wiring, voices, seeing signals, patches and MIDI.
help.why: The explanations here are about one thing at a time; the manual puts it all together.

new.title: NEW
new.what: Empties the rack: every module and cable goes.
new.does: Press it twice (it asks CLEAR ALL? first).
new.why: To start a patch from nothing. Save the one you have first if you want to keep it.

cables.title: Cables
cables.what: A cable carries a signal from an output (square jack) to an input (round jack).
cables.does: Click a jack, then another: an output and an input are joined. Click a plugged input to lift its cable and plug it somewhere else. An output can feed as many inputs as you like; an input takes one cable. A cable back up the chain makes a loop, which arrives one block (a third of a millisecond) late.
cables.why: In a modular synth the cables are the design: the same modules wired differently make completely different instruments.
try: Move one cable at a time and listen. Nothing can break: the worst that happens is silence or a loud noise (turn the Output's VOLUME down).

explain.title: These explanations
explain.what: Right-click any knob, button, jack or module header (or a module in + ADD MODULE, or a button in the top bar) to read about it here.
explain.does: Each explanation says what the thing is, how it works, why you'd want it, where it goes in a patch and what to try, with what it is doing on your rack right now: its value, what's plugged in, where its cable goes. Click a link to follow it; ◂ goes back.
explain.why: Hovering gives a line in the help bar; this gives the whole story, while you keep playing.
